findings.reason: README sequential rotate()/rotate(-2) example claims [1,2,3,4] instead of [2,3,4,1].

contentReview.behaviorReview: Validates before mutation; nonfinite infinity produces NaN remainder and is rejected. Modulo normalization rebuilds same-sized storage with original references; capacity remains untouched.
contentReview.retainedTestsReview: All pre-existing cases retained, new describe inserted between existing suites.

requiredRegressionReview.evidence: Default, positive/negative, zero, beyond-length counts and MAX_SAFE_INTEGER assert exact order and this.

Wrapped state explicitly asserted before rotating; subsequent peek/shift/pop/unshift/push/remove assert correct order. Capacity queue rotates and overflows both ends while asserting configured capacity and expected order.

Three objects are actually rotated, strict peekFront/peekBack equality checked against original references; invalid rotations preserve backing list/head/tail and values. Empty/singleton reuse covered.

contentReview.typesReview: rotate optional number returns this; default/negative/typed consumer cases supplied.
contentReview.docsReview: README explains directions, modulo, no-op and invalid-input errors. Its sequential example incorrectly claims [1,2,3,4] after rotate() then rotate(-2); task semantics and delivered test give [2,3,4,1].
